Build or change the RibbonScope scope, using the build-ribbon skill. Spec is the source of truth: read the spec, compare it with what's already built, and change the code to match.

# Scope

## Concept

### Pitch

The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

### Shape

#### Description

A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab component with its default styling. Its tabs are, in order: Project, Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups. There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

#### Groups

Each group has its title in small, muted text rotated -90deg (bottom to top) aligned along the left edge of the group naming what its commands have in common. Groups sit side by side, with a thin vertical divider between each.  The group label has a slightly different background color.

##### Project

A "Project" group holds the button for the [ProjectDirectoryScope](../reference/scope/project-directory/ProjectDirectoryScope.md).

##### Code

Nothing yet.

##### Spec

A "Build" group holds "Build Spec", which runs `piton build`.

##### Research

Nothing yet.

##### Application

An "Appearance" group holds the "Dark mode" switch, and a "Preferences" group holds "Settings", which opens the settings window.

A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

#### Commands

A command button shows a large icon above its label: a folder for the project, a hammer for Build Spec, and a gear for Settings. The project button reads "Open Project…" until a project is open, then the project's name. An on or off setting, like dark mode, is a switch rather than a button.
A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating its label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.
A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its tooltip says why: Build Spec is disabled until a project is open, and while the spec is building.

#### Height

The command area is the same height on every tab, even one with no commands, so the window beneath doesn't move when switching tabs.

#### Collapsing

The ribbon collapses to only its tabs, and expands again, with a chevron button at the right end of the tab bar, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1 (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Clicking a tab while the ribbon is collapsed selects it and expands the ribbon. Whether it is collapsed is saved for the user and restored on the next launch.

content.text:
I added a `BuildRibbon` skill and a `BuildRibbon` command to the spec. `piton check` and `piton build check` both pass, and a throwaway build produced both files. I didn't run `piton build` in the project itself, so `.claude/` doesn't have them yet.

- **Skill** (`spec/agent/skills/BuildRibbon.pi`): uses the existing `build-scope` template with `scope: {RibbonScope}`, exactly like `BuildApplication`. It builds to `.claude/skills/build-ribbon/SKILL.md`.
- **Command** (`spec/agent/commands/BuildRibbon.pi`): the spec had no command template, so I added one next to the skill template, `spec/lib/agent/commands/BuildScope.pi`. It defines the `build-scope-command` keyword.
  - It asks for the scope to be built or changed using the skill of the same name, with the spec as the source of truth.
  - It includes the Ribbon spec itself.
  - It builds to `.claude/commands/x-build-ribbon.md`, so you'd run it as `/x-build-ribbon`. Belay adds the `x-` to every command name; I checked and it happens even when the name doesn't clash with the skill.
- **Indexes:** `spec/agent/skills/index.pi` exports the new skill, a new `spec/agent/commands/index.pi` exports the command, and `spec/agent/index.pi` exports both folders.

The skill and the command can share the name `BuildRibbon` without colliding.

The Ribbon spec has changed since I built it: group titles are now rotated to run up the left edge, with a slightly different background. The code still centres them along the bottom, so running the command would change that.
